title: Sell Mineral Rights in Keenesburg, CO
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Keenesburg, CO | Weld County DJ Basin
metaDescription: Own minerals near Keenesburg in the Wattenberg field? We price your interest off decline data and recent comparable Weld County sales.
heroLead: Keenesburg sits in eastern Weld County, ground that has seen steady horizontal development as operators pushed drilling east from the tightest Wattenberg core over the past decade.
intro: Most owners we work with near Keenesburg hold interests tied to farm and ranch acreage where the mineral estate has been leased and, in many cases, produced for several years now. We start every conversation the same way: confirm your net revenue interest, pull trailing production, and fit a decline curve.

This part of Weld County has enough recent transaction history that we can check any decline-curve-based offer against real comparable sales, which gives owners here more pricing confidence than in less-developed parts of the basin.

sections.heading: Eastward development in the Wattenberg field
paragraphs: As the tightest core areas around Greeley and Fort Lupton have matured, operators have continued extending horizontal development east toward Keenesburg. Many tracts here have production histories that are a few years younger than the deepest core, which affects where they sit on the decline curve.

sections.heading: Pricing off your actual production
paragraphs: We fit a decline curve to your specific check stub history rather than assuming a standard timeline, since well age and initial production rate both affect how much value remains.

sections.heading: Checking against recent comparable sales
paragraphs: We weigh our decline-curve number against recent comparable transactions in this part of Weld County to make sure the offer reflects current market activity, not only a formula.

sections.heading: What to expect if your unit is relatively new
paragraphs: If your Keenesburg-area unit was drilled more recently than the deep Wattenberg core, your well may still be in its steeper early-decline phase rather than the long flat tail. That generally supports a stronger current offer, since more production life likely remains ahead of it.

faqs.question: Is Keenesburg-area production newer than the core Wattenberg field?
faqs.answer: Often somewhat, since operators extended development eastward over time, though there is still substantial production history to price against here.

faqs.question: What documents do you need to get started?
faqs.answer: A division order and a few recent check stubs let us begin pricing your interest right away.

faqs.question: How do you make sure the offer is fair?
faqs.answer: We check decline-curve pricing against recent comparable Weld County sales before finalizing any number.

faqs.question: How long does closing typically take?
faqs.answer: Two to four weeks once title is confirmed against Weld County records.

faqs.question: My well was drilled fairly recently. Does that mean a better offer?
faqs.answer: Often yes, since a newer well typically has more remaining production life ahead of it than one further along its decline curve.
